Getting Started > SAX3D 3D Asset Format and SLASL Shader Language Whitepaper
Status: Design whitepaper (2026-10-31, written by user order). Research is complete, all design forks have been decided (format forks F-1…F-7 and SLA macro forks J-1…J-8/F-3, of which F-5 was decided personally by the user, see the decision record in section eleven); both the SAX3D format implementation track and the SLA macro implementation track are in progress, and the format specification (SPEC) is not yet frozen — this page is a design finalization record, not a delivered format. Unproven surfaces declared up front: GLSL/HLSL artifacts' true compilation is unverified (this machine has no glslangValidator / dxc); Unity / Unreal / Blender have none truly compiled; volume comparison is being carried out by the implementation track, this page gives no volume numbers. Fact sources: the local research archives ~/workspace/sa3d-mesh-local/ (DESIGN / REPORT / validator prototype) and ~/workspace/sla-shader-local/ (DESIGN / REPORT / reference prototype), and four engine target archives plus the gpu-curtains and Shadertoy ecosystem archives.

1. Positioning: What SAX3D Is and Is Not

SAX3D is our self-developed 3D asset format and assembly language (named by the user on 2026-10-31 10:53): the model body is described with SA's type and layout discipline, the relations between mesh and materials, textures, and shaders are assembled with SAX-style layered declarations, and animation is a layer of the format from day one. Its reference is glTF — learning its layering and ecological niche, not targeting compatibility; it forms a pair with the shader language SLASL (section six): SLASL handles the shader layer, SAX3D handles the asset layer, and a material's shader slot references SLASL, with parameters bound by name to SLASL's interface table.

  • Is: an asset format (text assembly surface + binary payload surface), a binary schema pinned by SA declarations, a validation/compilation toolchain (Referee checks + resolution manifest output), and bidirectional converters with glTF/GLB (section eight).
  • Is not: not a renderer, not an engine, not a scene runtime, not an animation player. By analogy with the shader track's boundary set on 2026-10-31 09:54 (“only produce the corresponding shader files, the kernel should not include the whole engine”) and confirmed by the user's decision the same day: deliverables stop at files + toolchain; loading (reading a file into memory structures) belongs to the upper layer, not in sa_std (section nine).
  • Relation to existing stock: not a new vocabulary from scratch. sa_plugin_3dengines already holds the complete field layout of material descriptors (including per-slot texture references and vertex/fragment shader refs), the full vocabulary of animation clip/channel/sampler/player, a prototype decl node for scene, and hand-written SA implementations of glTF asset label and accessor layout validation — what is missing is exactly the declarative format + by-name assembly + compile-time checking layer; SAX3D supplies the format layer for the existing vocabulary. The sa_std graphics surface is zero (measured), and the three.js testbed's asset handling is JS object runtime assembly — both are negative baselines.

2. Migration of SAX Discipline: Five Pieces and Three Non-Migrations

The user's original question (2026-10-31 10:38) was “models described in SA, relations assembled with reference to SAX layered description”. Source-level mapping (sa_plugin_sax 1a88bf4's parser / lowerer / sax_rules + docs/sax_syntax.md inside sci) confirms: the essence of SAX style is five pieces of discipline, unrelated to the XML syntax skin, and this format adopts them wholesale:

The SAX FiveTheir Real Form in SAXTheir Landing Point in SAX3D
Closed vocabularyTags/attributes/events are all allow-listed, unknown means a named error SaxUnknownTagEach layer's declaration kinds and fields are closed sets, unknown field/kind = named error
Declaration tree<Component> nested element tree, the tree shape is the structureIn the assembly layer, scene node nesting is the parent-child relation (section four)
By-name slots<state> named state slots, the lowerer assigns deterministic offsetsAll cross-layer references by name; names are unique within their kind, duplicate names = named error
Referee named checkssax_rules five rules intercept out-of-bounds by nameThe validator gives named diagnostics item by item for dangling references, name/type mismatches, channel out-of-bounds (section five)
Resolution artifact (name → layout)Names resolve to a deterministic memory offset tableCompilation outputs a resolution manifest: each name → (kind, index, section, offset, layout), in hashable canonical form

Three non-migrations: the XML syntax skin (that is the shape of the DOM host surface, not the essence of assembly discipline); <state>'s runtime mutable semantics (assets are static descriptions, slots correspond to declaration items, not mutable state); event/handler binding (the asset layer has no events; its analogue is animation clip channels binding to nodes). One migrated after transformation: SAX's {expr} interpolation corresponds at the asset layer to literal parameter values (material parameters, transform values), likewise subject to the constraint of “can only reference declared names + type-checked”.

3. Geometry Described in SA

The literal landing point of “theoretical models can be described in SA”: the element types of geometry channels are SA types (f32, f32x2, f32x3, f32x4, u8x4, u16x4, u32, and other closed element type sets), and a binary section is the SA memory image of an array of that type (f32x3 = 3×f32 little-endian, no padding — SA scalar layout is exactly so). All record layouts are pinned verbatim by one SA declaration file distributed with the format specification, as the schema's sole source of truth: consumers in any language bind to that declaration and must not each compute offsets by hand (the hand-written accessor layout math in 3dengines proves hand computation is feasible, and also proves it should be taken in as a declaration). The binary header carries a version, with discipline following SAB's version gate: fields only added, never redefined. (That declaration file was provisionally named sam3d.sai in the research draft — the format was unnamed at the time; the formal file name will be finalized by the implementation track in the SPEC together with the SAX3D naming.)

  • Logical channel law (isomorphic to the SLASL logical slot law, Jev decision 1.0, see F-4 in section eleven): channels in the format are always independent tightly packed arrays (stride = element size, no padding, no interleaving); interleaved vertex layouts needed by consumers are derived at load/compile time per target, not written back into the format. Channel names are semantics; physical layout is not the author's business.
  • Canonical channel name set: position | normal | tangent | uv0..uv3 | color0 | joints0 | weights0, plus attr <name> custom channels allowed (element types must still be in the closed set). The canonical mapping from channels to shader @input is fixed by the format (position→position, uv<i>→uv/uv<i>, color0→color, joints0→joints, weights0→weights), and the validator checks accordingly that “every input the shader wants has a channel feeding it”.
  • A primitive is the unit of drawing and material binding, referencing a material by name; a mesh may have multiple primitives (v1 convention: primitives share all of the mesh's channels, subsetting is registered as a gap). Indices are optional; topology is a closed set (triangles default | triangle-strip | lines | line-strip | points). Optional bounds (min/max of the position channel, the counterpart of glTF accessor min/max).
  • morph targets: the geometry layer's morph block declares delta channels (deltas for position/normal/tangent); weights are not in the geometry layer — weights are an animation path or a runtime quantity; the morph name set is the component name order of the weight vector.

4. The Layered Model (Six Layers, Field Level)

Overall vocabulary discipline: each layer's declaration kinds and fields are closed sets; all cross-layer references are by name; information outside code such as sampler state and color space is always written explicitly in declarations, never guessed from file format, extension, or host defaults (the lesson of Shadertoy's channel externality: information outside code must be supplied by declarations).

4.1 Geometry Layer mesh

mesh <Name> {
    vertices <u32>;                                   // 顶点数（通道计数的锚）
    channel <chan> : <elem-type> @ <section>;         // 一条逻辑通道
    indices <u16|u32> @ <section> count <u32>;        // 可选
    primitive <pname> { material: <MaterialName>; }   // ≥1 个
    morph <mname> { channel <chan> : <elem-type> @ <section>; ... }   // 可选，增量通道
}

4.2 Skeleton Layer skeleton

skeleton <Name> {
    joint <JointName> { parent: <JointName>|none; bind: { t: [..]; r: [..]; s: [..]; } }
    ...
    inverse_bind @ <section>;        // f32x4x4 × joint 数，按声明序
}

A joint is a node of the assembly tree (same shape as glTF): skeleton only declares the joint name order (order = the logical index of the skinning matrix palette) and the inverse bind matrix section; joint hierarchy and transforms are borne in the assembly layer by same-named nodes; validation requires that each joint name has a same-named node in the assembly tree, and that the ancestor chain is consistent with the parent declaration. The elements of a mesh's joints0 channel are joint logical indices (u16x4, indexing the skeleton declaration order), consumers remap per target — the logical slot law again. weights0 and joints0 must appear in pairs (validation item).

4.3 Material Layer material

material <Name> {
    shader: <ShaderName>;                        // SLASL 产物引用（第六节）
    param <name> = <literal>;                    // 逐项按名对接口表 params 组
    texture <sampler-param-name>: <TextureName>;   // 按名绑纹理到 sampler 参数
    tex_transform <sampler-param-name> { offset: [u,v]; scale: [u,v]; rotation: f32; }  // 可选
    state { alpha: opaque|mask|blend; cutoff: f32; double_sided: bool; depth_write: bool; }
}

Binding checks are core discipline, see section five. state is a render state declaration (host-consumed, not shader semantics), its field set aligned with 3dengines' existing SA3D_MATERIAL_DESC stock. A material does not contain pipeline/blend equation details — that is the host renderer's business.

4.4 Texture Layer image / texture

image <Name> {
    source "path.png" | @ <section>;            // 外部文件 或 内嵌段
    format png|jpeg|ktx2|raw-rgba8|raw-rgba16f; // 载荷格式显式声明
    size <w> <h>;                               // raw 必填；容器格式可校验对读
    color_space srgb|linear;                    // 显式，永不猜
}
texture <Name> {
    image: <ImageName>;
    sampler { mag: nearest|linear; min: nearest|linear;
              mipmap: none|nearest|linear;
              wrap_u|wrap_v|wrap_w: clamp|repeat|mirror; }
}

image / texture / sampler are three separate pieces (isomorphic to glTF). v1 discipline: image payloads are opaque bytes to the format layer — PNG/JPEG decoding is not in the format layer (sa_std image codecs are missing, gap SAM3D-GAP-2); for raw formats, size and section length must match exactly, which the validator can verify.

4.5 Assembly Layer scene

scene <Name> {
    node <NodeName> {
        transform { t: [x,y,z]; r: [x,y,z,w]; s: [x,y,z]; }   // 或 matrix: [16 f32]，二选一，混写报错
        mesh: <MeshName>;
        material: <MaterialName>;        // 可选覆盖：仅当 mesh 单 primitive 时合法
        skin: <SkeletonName>;            // 可选
        node <ChildName> { ... }         // 嵌套即树
    }
}

The declaration tree is the assembly (isomorphic to SAX's declaration tree): nesting = parent-child, names are unique across the whole field (joint names and animation target names all resolve here). The closed set of optional node payloads (v1, Jev decision F-7 core_only 0.77): transform, mesh, material override, skin, child nodes; scene payloads such as cameras/lights already exist in 3dengines' decl kinds (CAMERA/LIGHT/PARTICLE), v1 does not enter the core with them, they are registered as extension candidates. The same mesh referenced by multiple nodes holds naturally (references by name, multiple references allowed); GPU instancing is not taken in v1 (gap SAM3D-GAP-5).

4.6 Animation Layer clip — a Clip Is an Action

clip <ClipName> {                                // 一个 clip 即一个「动作」
    sampler <SName> {
        input:  f32 @ <section> count <n>;       // 时间轴（秒，单调不减，校验项）
        output: <elem-type> @ <section> count <n>;
        interpolation: step|linear|cubic-spline;
    }
    channel { node: <NodeName>; path: translation|rotation|scale|weights; sampler: <SName>; }
}

The channel/sampler division is isomorphic to glTF and consistent with 3dengines' already-landed 3d_animation vocabulary, with only three changes: target by node name, sampler by in-clip name, input/output are section data references; cubic-spline output follows the glTF convention of triple packing (in-tangent, value, out-tangent), the validator checks section length by 3n. The output length for path: weights = the number of morphs of the target mesh, with name order corresponding. The format stores only clips: blending, transitions, state machines, and IK are all runtime matters (3dengines' player is already a runtime piece), explicitly drawn outside the format, and playback semantics must not be smuggled into the format. A clip's name is the action name, the host takes actions by name, and there is no ordering semantics between clips.

5. By-Name Binding and the Resolution Manifest

  • Names are the sole primary key (Jev decision F-3 name_primary 1.0): the author surface has only names; indices are compilation artifacts. glTF's “index references, name is only optional decoration” conflicts head-on with SAX style and is not adopted — reordering index references silently misaligns them, with no name to check, which is exactly what SAX style aims to eliminate. Ecosystem tools (Blender exporters, etc.) producing indices more conveniently is a cost for converters to digest, not a reason to change the format's primary key in reverse.
  • Material → SLASL binding contract: each param of a material must hit its shader interface table's params group by name + by type (f32↔scalar, vec2/3/4↔array literal, mat4↔16-element array); each texture binding's name must be a sampler parameter name in the interface table; sampler parameters in the interface table must not be left unbound, leaving one unbound = named error (same level as SAX's undeclared reference). For items in the params group that are not assigned a value: if the interface table carries a default value, use the default, otherwise error — silent zero values are not allowed (the default value contract itself is registered as gap SAM3D-GAP-7, to be finalized in alignment with the SLASL track).
  • What the asset layer must carry for this: a shader reference is not settled by a file path string — at compile time the asset compiler must obtain that shader's interface table artefact (a manifest produced by the SLASL compiler core, in hashable canonical form, generated from the same source, hand-writing forbidden, see 6.4); the correspondence between mesh channels and shader @input is given by the format-fixed canonical mapping table. Dependency direction: the asset compiler consumes the SLASL manifest, and does not in reverse require SLASL to know about assets — isomorphic to SAX's lowerer consuming the state slot table.
  • Resolution manifest: one compilation artifact is the asset manifest — each name → (kind, index, section, offset, layout) in hashable canonical form (hosts/upper-layer loaders build caches from it; same origin as the gpu-curtains and SLASL manifest precedents). This manifest is what section nine calls the “loading surface contract”: the format guarantees its completeness, and any upper-layer loader reading layouts from it will necessarily be consistent.
  • Validator prototype evidence (research-period reference implementation, not the production validator): the working example (a cube with 24 vertices, 1 primitive, 1 material, 1 texture, 1 SLASL shader reference, 1 rotation clip) actually ran VALIDATION OK, with section offsets 256 / 544 / 832 / 1024 / 1096 / 1112 / 1120 and total file length 1152 B matching the design layout table item by item; the negative control (injecting an undeclared param and an undeclared texture) produced two named errors and was judged FAILED — the checks are not decoration. The prototype's narrowings are registered item by item in the research archive (single-example grammar subset, section lengths taken from text declarations rather than real binaries, interface table played by a hand-made file, etc.), not masquerading as a production tool.

6. Shader: SLASL (A First-Class Chapter of SAX3D)

A material's shader slot is not settled by a reference — half of SAX3D's material semantics are defined on the shader side. This section is SLASL's design finalization record (user's supplementary order on 2026-10-31 11:13: shader fully included in this whitepaper as a first-class chapter). SLASL is unrelated to the cancelled sla2haxe direction (see the Haxe Compilation Backend: Can SA Become Haxe's Low-Level Compiler? page): that was about using SA as Haxe's low-level target; SLASL is a shader language developed for our own stack, hxsl-style, one source to multiple targets.

6.1 The SLASL Body: Typed Compilation from One Source to Multiple Targets

  • Form (set item by item by the user): 09:56 one source to multiple targets — the author writes one general shader (source extension .slasl, named SLASL at 09:57), sets a target, and generates that platform's shader file, a cross-compilation “similar to HLSL”; 09:54 only produces shader files, the kernel does not include the whole engine; 09:47 Unity / Unreal / Blender are first-class emission targets; 10:01 WebGPU is listed as a first-class target.
  • Pipeline (isomorphic to hxsl, with source evidence ring by ring): hxsl at Haxe compile time parses SRC block expressions (not strings) via MacroParser into a typed AST, checks them with the Checker, collects multiple fragments by priority, then goes through Linker (path merging + dependency graph) → Dce (component masks) → Flatten (logical packing) → each Out exclusively handling platform details. SLASL follows this layering: typed AST → fragment merging/linking (dependency-order weaving of init, same-name same-type variables unified) → component-level DCE → uniform logical packing → emission per target. Merging, DCE, and interface table generation are all completed in the target-independent layer; the target layer only does dialect transcription + convention wrapping + slot finalization.
  • Writing surface discipline: qualifiers follow hxsl — @global (host-level quantities shared by all fragments, declarable in groups, accessed qualified by group name), @input (vertex input), @param (this material's parameters), @const (compile-time constants, the sole source of variants), @range. Sampling is written method-style as tex.get(uv) — the AST is a sampling operation node, dialect transcription is exclusively the backend's; if user code contains layout / binding / precision / version numbers / register, it is a named check error — zero leakage of platform details (the hxsl iron rule). A shader is not a string, and a runtime builder is not used as the main surface (already decided by the user: the string form has zero compile-time checking, merging can only be text pasting).
  • Artifacts are only files: the compiler core (AST schema, checker, linker, emitters) is a code production capability of std/the toolchain, run by build steps/the asset pipeline; the rendering runtime (program/uniform/texture handles, contexts, windows, material systems, scenes, drivers) is explicitly excluded from std.

6.2 Target Registry

The registry has two layers: dialect backends (AST→dialect text) and the host convention layer (wrapping structure, same-package files, binding finalization, variant translation). Adding a target = adding one layer, without touching the writing surface or the merging layer.

LayerTargetKey Points and Hard Contracts
DialectGLSL ES 3.00 / GLSL ES 1.00Prototype landed (evidence in section eight); std140 and layout slot finalization / texture2D and precision, attribute/varying, no UBO
DialectHLSL (SM5 form)Prototype landed; cbuffer + register finalization, .Sample(), SV_* semantics
DialectWGSL (WebGPU first-class)Dialect + thin convention layer, the host is the WebGPU API itself; six finalizations see 6.4
DialectMSLOur newly added backend — fact correction: heaps master has only GlslOut/HlslOut/NXGlslOut, no MetalOut, not masquerading as a replica (registered D-1)
DialectSPIR-VRegistered later: hosts (the Vulkan/Blender Vulkan road) mostly bring their own GLSL→SPIR-V, our direct emission benefit is lowest
ConventionunityEmission unit = a complete ShaderLab asset; all material properties enter the sole CBUFFER_START(UnityPerMaterial), the same copy for all Passes; textures go via the TEXTURE2D/SAMPLER macro triple, outside the CBUFFER; violating the SRP Batcher is a silent performance demotion that compilation cannot detect — the generator must self-check with a manifest
Conventionunreal-globalDelivery definition = paired (three-piece) production: .usf + optional .ush + C++ glue (FGlobalShader subclass, parameter structure, registration macro four-way binding); parameters and C++ structure members verbatim same-named, layout obeys engine macro reflection packing, self-emitted register()/hand-written cbuffer forbidden; first landing point = global shader, compute first; the material surface belongs to engine code generation, we do not generate mesh materials
ConventionblenderArtifacts are a two-piece set = info-equivalent declaration + dialect source; interface first (slots explicitly declared on the info side); source must not carry its own #version (host-injected); borrow its declaration/binding contract, do not depend on its text collage (Blender itself has no AST-level merging)

6.3 The Logical Slot Law and Variant Grading (Cross-Target Iron Rules)

  • Logical slot law: AST-layer resource slots are always logical slots — the globals group and params group are each flattened into a logical layout (each field records an (offset, size) logical slot, textures/samplers record logical slot numbers); physical binding (GLSL layout(binding), HLSL register, WGSL @group/@binding, Metal index partitioning, Blender's Metal rearrangement partitioning) is finalized by the target layer. Evidence: the same logical slot has different physical arrangements under Blender's GL/Vulkan/Metal; this is exactly the same-origin discipline as SAX3D section three's logical channel law.
  • Variant grading: the sole source of variants is @const, the target layer only translates, inventing no new dimensions, and grades by the target's variant budget — bare dialects produce multiple files by variant key at link time; WebGPU has no preprocessor available, so it goes via override / module splitting (6.4 item 5); Unity grades into host tiers such as shader_feature_local (keyword item budget 256, local ≤64/shader, variant count audit before emission with a note beside the artifact); Unreal is a C++ permutation dimension class (closed value sets + ShouldCompilePermutation filtering + total budget alarm), dimension classes are generated by us and are part of the file artifacts. @const combinations exceeding the budget must be demoted to runtime branches or loudly error, silent expansion is not allowed.
  • Backend capability discipline: AST nodes unsupported by a backend are named-rejected at emission time as UnsupportedInBackend, demotion rewriting is not allowed; sampling/derivative nodes carry control-flow consistency annotations, and merging and DCE must not make a sampling point cross a consistency boundary (WGSL is a hard gate, other dialects are portability discipline).

6.4 The Binding Contract with SAX3D

  • The interface table is an artifact after merging/DCE: LinkedShader carries an interface table — the logical layouts of the globals group and params group, the texture logical slot table, the input table, the varying table, variant keys. Items eliminated by DCE disappear from the interface table at the same time (the prototype gold file layout comparison is an instance: the Params block contains the two fields base_color / tint, dead_weight is no longer in the table). SAX3D materials' params bind to this table by name + by type, mesh channels feed @input by canonical name, sampler unbinding loudly errors — for the full contract, see section five.
  • WebGPU surface same-package constraints (the essentials of the six finalizations): ① binding is a bilateral contract with canonical hard budgets (bind group ≤4, uniform 12/stage, storage 8/stage, sampled textures/samplers 16 each/stage, single uniform binding ≤64KiB, offset 256B alignment, etc.), exceeding the budget fails loudly and names the over-limit item; ② combined samplers split in WGSL into texture + sampler two slots, with the pairing relation entering the manifest; ③ the browser JS host has a zero-reflection interface, so the reflection manifest is a mandatory same-package piece — emitted together with the .wgsl (entry point static access sets, buffer byte layout tables, overrides, required features/limits, sampler pairings, entry IO), generated from the same source as the artifact, hand-maintained maintenance forbidden, and designed as a hashable canonical form for the host to build/cache pipeline layouts; ④ interface metadata is single-source triple-generated (WGSL declaration segments, binding manifests, and layout offset tables derived from the same source, never separately maintained), and for members whose layout deviates from WGSL's bare defaults the emitter must emit @align/@size to pin them; ⑤ variants have only the override road (scalar conditions go via override with @id stable key names, those changing the resource interface/entry signature/stage composition split into multiple .wgsl modules); ⑥ implicit derivative sampling consistency ownership is annotated at the AST layer and rechecked after merging, violations error at compile time. The true acceptance gate = building a pipeline per the manifest layout (createShaderModule never throwing is not an acceptance gate).

6.5 Bidirectional Ecology: Existing Shaders Back to SLASL

  • Form general rule (set by the user on 2026-10-31 10:13): importers are always local conversion tools, single-piece conversions manually initiated by the user — no API client, key management, bulk fetching, or indexing service for any source (the bidirectional expansion at 10:06 is executed under this caliber). The user provides their own shader code (obtained by themselves from sites etc.), and converts it piece by piece with the tool; conversion happens on the user side, targeting the user's own code, and the tool itself carries no content license.
  • Architectural symmetry: one importer frontend per source dialect (parsing → the same typed AST + interface table recovery), sharing the AST/interface table with the forward target backends — the AST is the bidirectional hub. Artifacts must pass the same SLASL checker rule set; constructions outside the subset are loudly rejected (named diagnostic UNSUPPORTED <来源>:<构造> + source position), silent approximation is not allowed. Round-trip discipline: source→SLASL→source target compared item by item on the equivalence surfaces of declaration sets/interface tables/computation graphs; acceptance requires multiple frames + input sanitization, numeric readings promise only tolerance pixel comparison from headless WebGL2 true rendering, not bit-for-bit equivalence.
  • Shadertoy first: its real form = one GLSL ES frontend + one layer of host contract shim (the contract layer is small and fully mechanical, the language layer is a true frontend of the same order as the forward compiler: ES 3.00 grammar as the skeleton + ES 1.00 alias/tolerance layer). The number-one mechanical constraint is channel externality: iChannel0..3's sampler dimensions (2D/Cube/3D), filter/wrap, and pass ownership are only in the page configuration, not decidable from code — supplied by the user at conversion time via a declaration configuration (the field set uses its API JSON's full field set as reference), undeclared ones are loudly marked “untyped” and guessing is refused. The full standard uniform table enters the interface table as reserved host items; Common is AST-merged at link time into each consumer pass; self-feedback is a property of the pass graph layer, not entering a single pass's AST; mainSound is a non-fragment entry kind, loudly unsupported in the first version (entry kind gap). Coverage is an engineering estimate (not a census): Image-only about 70–85%, with Common about 65–80%, with the premise including the expansion road for function-like #define macros (J-8 decided as graded mixing, see 6.6).
  • Blender second: create-info carries its own interface metadata; at import, logical slots and parameter tables are recovered on its basis, bidirectionally same-origin with the forward info piece; node-generated code is machine-generated text with low import value, registered for later. Unreal self-contained USF subset last: only those with explicit parameter structures and self-contained entries are taken; code depending on engine .ush semantics is outside the subset and named-rejected; when a permutation define set is closed and enumerable it maps to @const, when not enumerable that dimension is rejected. Phasing discipline: learn to write first, then to read — the import direction is queued after forward GLSL/HLSL production.

6.6 Enabling Layer: SLA Macro Improvements (SLASL's Foundation, Brief)

SLASL's writing surface as a whole is built on SLA's macro and other metaprogramming support — hxsl's full capability is built on Haxe's compile-time macros (syntax as data + typed checking), which is the root judgment after comparing the two sides. Mapping evidence (source + eight probe corpora): SLA currently has two macro worlds + one fixed-purpose template facility, with sharply different capability boundaries — SLA-layer user macros have AST statement templates as macro bodies, but parameters are already-evaluated expressions, calls are always void, there are no syntax parameters, they cannot be called in declaration position, macro bodies cannot contain declarations, and authors cannot read argument types; SA-layer import macros ([MACRO]) analyze at the text layer, can take labels as parameters, and by borrowing the leading output convention can be used as expressions (in clear asymmetry with user macros); @expand_tuple is the sole declaration generation facility, with a closed vocabulary and type blindness. Using hxsl's needs as the ruler, gaps SLA-SHADER-GAP-1…7 are registered (syntax as data / declaration-level generation / in-macro type visibility / expression-position user macros / compile-time evaluation / identifier construction / checker intervention points); classification conclusion: all blocking gaps are absences of language design, not implementation bugs — the current macro machine is a complete finished product for its established design, so there is no purely implementational gap that can be prototyped unilaterally, and all are packaged and sent to Jev for decision.

Jev's nine decisions (2026-10-31, jev-1.14.0; full text stored at ~/workspace/jev-designs/slasl_macro_ruling.json; the macro implementation track is implementing per this): J-1 syntax as data = declaration-level sublanguage registration 0.68 (syntax parameters 0.07, attribute transformation hooks 0.01, syntax+registration combination 0.24) — new declaration kinds are handled by registered sub-parsers (such as shader declarations), this is SLASL's minimal surface, and the reference prototype has independently verified this semantics; J-2 declaration-level generation = merged into J-1 (0.71); J-3 in-macro type visibility = macro parameters may declare types (0.75); J-4 expression-position user macros = copying the import macros' leading output convention (0.77); J-5 checker intervention points = an independent read-only check hook (0.93); J-7 link execution point = std library production as the semantic benchmark 0.99 (the linker is ordinary SLA library code, run by the build/asset pipeline, static linking inside a plugin is only registered as an optional optimization); J-6 compile-time evaluation = general improvement deferred, not blocking (0.80); F-3 output form = hxsl-style structured output group (0.78, the prototype's special names are only transitional); J-8 Shadertoy function-like #define macro road = graded mixing 0.68 (object-like constant macros keep structural mapping, function-like macros are expanded in the first version with traces left in the artifact; full expansion for coverage 0.25, full fidelity for structure 0.07).

6.7 Prototype Evidence and Unproven Surfaces (Truthful)

  • Reference prototype evidence (Zig reference implementation: frontend sub-parser + checker subset + linker + GLSL ES 3.00 / ES 1.00 / HLSL three emitters): input base.slasl + tint.slasl two fragments, producing 8 gold files byte-for-byte identical (rebuild + rerun + per-file diff all equal counts as PASS), with four demonstration points holding item by item: ① init written out of order, dependency order corrected after linking (tint_boost before tint_pre); ② same-name same-type @param unified across fragments into the same Params block; ③ DCE makes the Params layout 48 → 32 bytes — dead_weight and scratch disappear simultaneously from the AST, the parameter layout, and all backend artifacts (grep zero hits), with the eliminated segment listed by name; ④ sampling translated three ways — tex.get(v_uv) → ES 3.00 texture() / ES 1.00 texture2D() / HLSL tex.Sample(tex_sampler, v_uv); @const conditions already folded at link time (no residual if in the three artifacts). The macro mapping eight probes rerun 8/8 consistent with the registration, serving as the language batch's “before improvement” baseline corpus.
  • Prototype narrowings registered item by item, not masquerading as the target form: type/statement subset, no helper functions or let, no multiple render targets, init weaving covers only var dependencies, DCE component masks only to swizzle read-set granularity, HLSL only SM5 form, output uses special names (F-3 has decided the structured group, form pending), the import direction is entirely outside the prototype.
  • Unproven surfaces: GLSL/HLSL artifacts' true compilation unproven (this machine has no glslangValidator / dxc); Unity has no editor true compilation, Unreal is unverifiable on this machine (source license gated), Blender has no built binary true verification — the three houses' acceptance calibers are written per their respective ceilings, not masquerading as verified; on the WebGPU side, headless Chrome's module-level legal path has been proven by the archive track, pipeline-level (L3) acceptance has not been run on this machine.

7. Container Dual Forms: Split, Merged, and External References

The user set on 2026-10-31 10:56: “We want flexibility, learn from glTF, have both text and binary, can split and import, for example sa mesh and slasl placed externally, assembled by sax; there can also be one merged binary.” Accordingly, the container's dual forms are both first-class — two packagings of the same asset, not two formats (this decision overrides the research draft's old F-2 form which registered the merged form only as a later candidate; Jev's 1.0 decision for the split form does not contradict the split form being the authoring form):

  • Split form (authoring form): the assembly text externally references independent files by name/path — SA mesh binaries (geometry section files), .slasl shader files, texture files; the assembly layer only does referencing and binding (analogous to glTF's .gltf referencing .bin and images). The text surface is subject to the closed vocabulary + type checking (the binary surface's schema is pinned by SA declarations, see section three) — this is exactly the dividing line from glTF's “JSON with no schema, validation relying on an external validator”.
  • Merged form (delivery form): a single-file binary (GLB analogy: header + section table + embedded assembly text section + all payload sections), version gate discipline following SAB: the header carries a version, fields only added, never redefined.
  • Packer: split form → merged form is a toolchain piece; dual-form equivalence is an acceptance item — the two examples (the cube example and the skinned animation example) each go through both forms, and the section set unpacked from the merged form is section-by-section equivalent to the split form (offsets may differ, content byte-for-byte the same), and the validator gives the same Referee conclusion for both forms. In the merged form, shaders are registered by reference name as the baseline.

8. The SAX3D ↔ glTF/GLB Bidirectional Converter

The user ordered on 2026-10-31 11:04: “Add one more converter, sax3d to gltf glb convert mutually.” The converter is queued in the batch immediately following format finalization (SPEC freeze) (this order implements Jev F-6's right_after_format 0.58 as decided work, and expands it from one-way import to bidirectional); the mapping table comes first — listing construction by construction what is adopted / approximated / loudly unsupported, table before code.

  • Inbound (glTF/GLB → SAX3D): buffers/accessors → independent tight channels (interleaved layouts are split back into independent channels on the inbound side, the logical channel law does not yield); index references are renamed to name primary keys; nodes/skins/animations/morph are named per the isomorphic mapping in the design. glTF materials have no shader concept: their PBR parameter set maps to SAX3D material parameters, and the disposition of the shader slot (binding a named standard PBR SLASL material shader, or explicitly marking it unbound) must be fixed in the mapping document with reasons given, silence is not allowed.
  • Outbound (SAX3D → glTF/GLB): produces both .gltf+.bin and .glb forms. The material parameter set is approximated to glTF PBR per the mapping table; an SLASL shader reference has no counterpart on that side — together with all other constructions without counterparts, it must item by item enter the conversion report (what was approximated and why; what was omitted and why), zero silent loss is a hard acceptance item.
  • Acceptance: round-trip equivalence — glTF→SAX3D→glTF semantic equivalence (geometry bytes the same, material parameters per the mapping table, animation channels the same), and likewise for SAX3D→glTF→SAX3D on the SAX3D-expressible subset; the asset set = the two working examples + at least one real-world glTF sample. If conversion forces out a format defect, register it as a defect and stop reporting, do not work around it inside the converter.
  • Inbound stock: 3dengines' 3d_gltf already has a complete hand-written SA implementation of accessor layout math that can be reused; what is missing is JSON parsing + the full mapper (gap SAM3D-GAP-3).

9. The Boundary Between Format and Loading

The user personally decided on 2026-10-31 10:53 (F-5, not sent to Jev): “No, std is the bottom layer, everything loaded is an upper layer.” — sa_std does not hold a SAX3D reference loading library; all loading pieces belong to the upper layer (host/application side, the upper plugin layer is also included). Reinforced rationale at 10:54: “glTF also has no built-in loader, we can just refer to it” — the reference precedent points the same way: glTF has only a format specification, loaders are all in the ecosystem's upper layers; SAX3D proceeds likewise.

  • This decision aligns with the existing doctrine that “cores enter std, plugins only wrap/frame”: loading is not a bottom-layer core. Note the boundary with SLASL is not to be confused — the SLASL compiler core enters std/the toolchain because it is a code production capability (input source code, output files); a loader is a runtime piece (input files, output memory structures for running), and the two are separate in the layering.
  • The format side's responsibility stops at: guaranteeing the loading surface contract is complete — i.e., section five's resolution manifest (name→layout) is produced with compilation and is in hashable canonical form, so that layouts read by any upper-layer loader from it are consistent. In which layer a loader is written, and in what language, is the upper layer's own business.

10. Volume Rationale (Mechanism Statement + Measured Comparison, 2026-10-31)

The user pointed out on 2026-10-31 10:57: “In theory we are much smaller than the glTF and GLB formats, because we do not need excessive JSON description.” The mechanism holds, stated item by item as follows — this is design rationale, not a measurement conclusion:

  • Our record layouts are pinned by a shared single SA schema declaration, distributed with the specification, not carried with each asset; glTF/GLB, by contrast, makes each asset carry the full set of JSON descriptions — the key names and structures of accessor / bufferView / material / node objects repeated item by item.
  • References inside the merged form are compiled indices, names appearing only once in the name table; the text authoring form exists only on the author side and does not enter the delivery payload.
  • Honest boundary: for large assets dominated by geometry payloads, both sides' payload bytes are the same — what is saved is the descriptive overhead; the smaller the asset and the more objects it has, the larger the gap.
  • Status: measured comparison in progress — the implementation track in acceptance produces glTF (.gltf+.bin) and GLB reference pieces from the same cube example, comparing bytes item by item against SAX3D's split/merged forms (total length + descriptive overhead/geometry payload listed separately). Before the numbers come out, this page pre-prints no volume figures.

Measured results (2026-10-31, comparison produced): the same cube example — SAX3D merged form 2,303 B, GLB 2,584 B, glTF (.gltf+.bin) 2,554 B: the merged form's total length is smaller by 10.9%, of which the descriptive overhead is smaller by 12.9% (geometry payloads are the same on both sides; what is saved is exactly the descriptive overhead the mechanism statement points to). The split form is 3,441 B, of which over 1,300 B are teaching comments, not format overhead. The earlier magnitude expectation of “much smaller” does not hold; this page takes the measurement as authoritative.

  • Implementation: delivered (2026-10-31, staging awaiting integration). The SPEC is frozen (deviation register D-1…D-8 on record): schema single source (sax3d.sai → generated shared tables), block-style parsing + Referee validator (text 35 + binary 7 diagnostic codes, all loud), binary writing (version gate header + section table + trailing name table), deterministic packing (split and merged forms' section contents byte-for-byte equivalent). Acceptance tests/run_tests.sh 62/62; the bidirectional converter delivered with it, tests/run_convert.sh 24/24, the failing name set empty; the cube example's section offsets match design §8 item by item, the hero skinned example passes, 22 negative examples' first diagnostics hit precisely. The read-back validator is a test-only piece and does not constitute a loader distributed with the format (section nine boundary unchanged).

Conversion reported three format facts: ① v1 primitives have no index ranges, multi-primitive export has drawing overlap (first candidate for SPEC evolution); ② raw-rgba16f has no lossless glTF form, the converter loudly rejects it; ③ texture slots are determined by the shader interface.
  • Version gate (verified): binary header offset 8 is version_major: u16 = 1, offset 10 is version_minor: u16 = 0 (pinned by sax3d.sai); the reader gate loudly rejects major ≠ 1 (Sax3dUnsupportedVersion); the text form requires exactly one asset <Name> version 1; header. Evolution discipline: additive changes minor +1, semantic redefinitions major +1.
  • The merged-form shader name-recording fork (design §6.4) has been decided: Jev decided keep_name_only 0.48 (confidence 0.22, explicitly noted as overturnable) — in the merged form shaders are registered by name only, source not embedded, adopted and executed by default; an optional source-embedding batch will be proposed separately only when an archiving need appears.
